summary:
ORBITCARE is an astronaut-centered health monitoring prototype for long-duration space missions. It brings together recorded physiological measurements, self-reported sleep, fatigue, stress, symptoms, countermeasure checklists, alerts, medical records, and mission events in one secure dashboard.

The platform helps astronauts evaluate their own health by comparing current measurements with their personal historical baseline using transparent median-and-MAD trend analysis. Its interactive digital twin visualizes recorded cardiovascular, respiratory, sleep, musculoskeletal, thermal, and radiation-context signals. A built-in evidence-grounded assistant can summarize changes, explain alerts, and point users to supporting records without making diagnoses or treatment recommendations.

ORBITCARE addresses the Health Monitoring Software challenge by turning fragmented health indicators into understandable, actionable mission context. It clearly labels synthetic versus real/reference data, supports NASA OSDR dataset ingestion, preserves auditability, and keeps medical decisions human-led.
details:
ORBITCARE is an astronaut-centered health-monitoring web application for long-duration space missions. It combines recorded vital signs, daily self-reports, countermeasure tracking, alerts, medical records, and mission events in one dashboard. The system compares current readings with each astronaut’s own historical baseline using transparent median and median-absolute-deviation analysis, helping users identify changes that need review without claiming diagnosis or flight clearance.

The platform includes interactive trend charts, a data-driven digital twin, role-based astronaut and medical-officer access, audit logging, downloadable reports, and an evidence-grounded mission-health assistant. It is built with React, TypeScript, Vite, FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and SQLite, with optional Firebase synchronization. The architecture supports locally reviewed NASA OSDR reference-data imports and clearly labels synthetic versus reference data.

Super Intelligence tools were used for ideation, coding/debugging, and writing/editing during development. No SI-generated images, video, or audio are included. The in-app assistant is constrained to project records and safety limitations.
